decisive_items: cystic background with “dirty” necrosis and pseudopapillary clusters of moderately atypical cells with cyanophilic cytoplasm
category V (suspicious for malignancy) by the Milan System
homogeneously enhancing nodular lesion in the superficial lobe of the right parotid gland, surrounded by a thin fibrous capsule, with no suspicious cervical lymph nodes or thoracic lesions
response.rationale: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma best fits a cystic parotid mass with suspicious cytology and a well-circumscribed enhancing nodule without nodal or distant disease. Warthin tumor and pleomorphic adenoma are contradicted by Milan category V and atypical cells; salivary duct carcinoma is less likely given the thin capsule and absence of aggressive infiltrative features.

rejected.why: Benign Warthin tumor cannot explain Milan category V suspicious cytology with atypical pseudopapillary clusters; smoking and cystic debris are nonspecific.
Pleomorphic adenoma is typically solid and well-defined, and is contradicted by cystic dirty necrosis and suspicious cytology.

Salivary duct carcinoma was initially considered but is a high-grade aggressive tumor; the homogeneously enhancing thin-capsule nodule without nodal or thoracic disease favors a low-grade malignancy such as mucoepidermoid carcinoma.
